tags.definition: Catch-all for B2B / Enterprise feedback; use when no other b2b-xx applies.

Everything that happens after the Team seat purchase to get the team's seats and access actually working, excluding personal-to-team migration/visibility issues and day-to-day admin/governance configuration. Specifically covers: initial Team workspace setup and vendor procurement coordination; two distinct invite failure modes — the invite email/code never being delivered at all, and an invite being delivered but joining/access still failing; an admin losing access to the whole team's backend after deleting a prior admin account (an access-recovery scenario, not a governance configuration); the product gap where the admin/billing contact's own email consumes a full paid seat with no free manage-only role; and whether one purchased license can be shared across multiple devices or users.
positive_examples: 'needs vendor onboarding documents to proceed with a team purchase'
'how to set up a Team plan with multiple seats'

mece_rules.reason: Admin & Group Controls (ongoing governance, not initial setup)
License Sharing & Multi-Device (consumer multi-device, not formal team)

tags.definition: Admin/governance needs for teams — centralized admin, member/permission management, data-sharing controls across an org.
positive_examples: 'wants centralized IT admin and data-sharing controls for 25-50 devices'
'cannot prevent cross-department data sharing in Team plan'

negative_examples.example: 'how do I create the team account?'

tags.definition: Covers every decision-support inquiry a prospect raises before committing to buy a Team plan, in two parts: (1) pricing and quotation itself -- minimum seat requirements, per-seat pricing rules, currency confusion (e.g. SGD/USD), volume/bulk pricing, and requests for a formal quote/PDF for internal procurement approval; and (2) plan-fit capability evaluation -- whether every team member needs their own hardware device, whether recordings are private by default and whether an admin can see members' recordings, how Team differs from Personal/Unlimited plans in features and benefits, and what admin control capabilities the Team plan offers. All of these occur while the prospect has not yet committed to purchase and is still evaluating.
positive_examples: 'How many seats are required at minimum to start a Team plan'
'Asks whether bulk seat purchases qualify for dedicated discount pricing'

negative_examples.example: 'cannot find where to download my invoice'

tags.definition: Invoicing and tax/procurement documentation enterprise buyers need around a Team purchase, typically owned by Finance/Procurement rather than Product. Covers post-purchase invoice corrections (company name/VAT, B2C-to-B2B conversion) and pre-purchase requests for a purchase order (PO), tax-exempt proof, or a W-9 form
positive_examples: "Needs a Team invoice updated with VAT number and company details"
"Requests a DPA after purchase the Team plan"

negative_examples.example: 'how do I set up a Team plan?'

tags.definition: Compliance and certification documents enterprise buyers require before they can purchase or renew Team, typically owned by Legal/Privacy rather than Product -- response latency here directly determines whether a deal can proceed. Covers HIPAA/BAA for healthcare use, a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) and GDPR/EU data-residency confirmation, and SSO single-sign-on requirements. Note: DPA is currently Team-only, which itself pushes some solo/regulated users toward Team just to obtain it.
positive_examples: 'Is Plaud Team GDPR compliant?'

negative_examples.example: 'requests GDPR DPA and EU data residency'

negative_examples.example: 'how do I use the device I already own?'

tags.definition: Issue not actually resolved, or resolution poor/generic (distinct from response speed).
positive_examples: 'support replied but issue never resolved'
'resolution was poor/generic'

tags.definition: Self-service help content (help center, docs, FAQ, in-box manual) is missing, incomplete, or users cannot find the answer — distinct from a user directly asking support.
positive_examples: 'cannot find help documentation / FAQ for this'
'knowledge base does not cover my issue'

mece_rules.reason: Product & Usage Questions (user asks support directly = inbound enquiry)

negative_examples.example: 'how do I use feature X?' asked to support

tags.definition: Catch-all for Software & App complaints; use when no other sw-xx tag applies.
Confirmed app freezes/crashes or gets stuck during syncing, generating, exporting, or other core workflows.
positive_examples: 'App crashes every time I try to open a recording'

mece_rules.reason: cloud sync failures, not app runtime

tags.definition: User expects USB transfer; confirmed feature is unavailable on their model/plan or does not work as designed despite following official instructions.
positive_examples: 'Feedback concentrated on strong backlash following USB direct-transfer feature removal in Note firmware v2.2.'

mece_rules.reason: Fast Transfer (local WiFi file transfer, not cloud)

tags.definition: Confirmed file transfer/export fails (USB/app/desktop) due to software issues such as errors, timeouts, or incomplete transfers.
positive_examples: 'Wi-Fi transfer fails'

mece_rules.reason: Fast Transfer (local WiFi file transfer, not cloud)

tags.definition: Confirmed recordings cannot be accessed/recovered (missing files, failed sync, corrupted storage) after standard recovery steps.
positive_examples: 'My recording was crashed. Can'tretrieve my recording'

mece_rules.reason: Fast Transfer (local WiFi file transfer, not cloud)

tags.definition: Confirmed playback fails or is abnormal (no sound, stutter, file won’t play) across supported players/apps.
The operation flow works but is tedious, inefficient, or stressful — too many steps, repetitive manual actions, high effort to finish a task.
positive_examples: 'Too many steps to export files'

tags.definition: User reports instructions/guide are unclear, incomplete, or misleading for setup or core tasks.
positive_examples: 'The navigation is confusing — can't find where to export files'

tags.definition: Incorrect or missing translations in the app interface, language-switching failures, or non-English UI unexpectedly displaying in English.
positive_examples: 'German translation is incorrect in the settings menu'

mece_rules.reason: Translation (content translation of recordings, not app interface language)

tags.definition: Hardware-to-app connectivity and transfer reliability — is the connection smooth, does the recording actually transfer over (WiFi upload or Bluetooth upload), and is it fast enough. Also owns OTA firmware download/transfer to the device (stuck/failed/slow OTA), since that's the same transfer-channel question.
positive_examples: ‘Recordings sit undelivered over WiFi despite a fine connection’;
‘Bluetooth upload much slower than before‘;
’pairs over BT but transfer stalls/fails partway’;
‘OTA download stuck at a percentage; unclear/unreliable whether upload goes over WiFi or Bluetooth.’

tags.definition: Recording initiation and control issues not covered by more specific tags: unexpected auto-start, inability to change recording mode, or recording process control bugs. Distinct from hardware-level silent recording.
positive_examples: 'The in-app recording pause button is missing / doesn't work'

mece_rules.reason: recording completes but file is silent

tags.definition: Cloud sync failures, uploads stuck, recordings showing as 'locked,' or data inconsistencies across devices.
positive_examples: 'Recordings show as locked and won't open'

mece_rules.reason: Fast Transfer (local WiFi file transfer, not cloud)

tags.definition: Post-processing editing issues: transcript edits not saving, content reverting after reopening, inability to rename recordings.
positive_examples: 'Edits to the transcript don't save — it reverts every time I reopen the file'

mece_rules.reason: App Performance & Stability (app crashes/freezes in general, not specifically edit-save failures)

tags.definition: Issues exporting or sharing recordings, transcripts, or summaries: unsupported formats, export failures, expiring share links, speaker labels lost in export.
positive_examples: 'Can't export the transcript as a DOCX file'

mece_rules.reason: Cloud & Sync (cloud sync failures, not intentional export/share actions)

tags.definition: Asset-attribution axis: device, membership, or data are attached to the 'wrong' account (device bound to another/old account, subscription on wrong account, data in another account, duplicate/split accounts). Login itself may work — the problem is the asset-to-account mapping.
positive_examples: 'Second-hand device says linked to another account'
'Membership shows on my purchase email but not my login email'
'Recordings disappeared after logging into another account'
'Two accounts from the same email via different login methods'

mece_rules.reason: Same-account cloud sync failure -> Cloud & Sync
Has access, only re-binding a device -> Device Management
Subscription status sync on the SAME account -> Monetization

negative_examples.example: 'Bluetooth pairing fails though account is fine'
'Paid on same account but plan shows expired'
'Recordings fail to sync to cloud on same account'

tags.definition: Rule-based automation ("when X happens, do Y") issues: rules not triggering, unexpected default behavior, or automation action errors. Distinct from AI Agent actions.
positive_examples: 'Set up Autoflow to send summaries by email but it never triggers'

mece_rules.reason: Integration (third-party tool connection issues, not automation rule logic)

tags.definition: Third-party tool integrations (Notion, Slack, Zoom, Salesforce, HubSpot, Zapier, etc.) failing to connect, syncing inconsistently, or requests for new integration support.
positive_examples: 'Notion integration keeps disconnecting — syncs about 50% of the time'

mece_rules.reason: Autoflow (automation rule logic, not the connection itself)
API (developer API/webhook issues, not end-user integration)

negative_examples.example: 'API key not working for our custom integration'

tags.definition: API key access, Webhook configuration, or OAuth integration technical issues and developer requests.
positive_examples: 'Need an API key to integrate Plaud with our internal system'

mece_rules.reason: Integration (end-user third-party tool connections, not developer API)

tags.definition: Compatibility issues across iPad, multi-screen layouts, or different OS versions (iOS/Android).
positive_examples: 'iPad app doesn't support split-screen mode'

tags.definition: Recording phone/VoIP calls — capability or failures (only own voice, no auto-detect).
positive_examples: 'other party's voice not recorded on phone calls'

tags.definition:
Personal < -> Team migration/visibility issues. 
A Team workspace is PLAUD's collaborative workspace for businesses, serving as a governed container for team collaboration, admin controls, billing, and data boundaries
It allows organizations to create a shared workspace, invite and manage team members, handle billing, manage security and offboarding, and collaborate on meeting content together. Each seat includes full Plaud Unlimited Plan benefits, and it's priced per seat with a minimum of 2 seats required for sign-up.
positive_examples: 'switching between Personal and Team workspaces'
'Manage the workspace via Settings'

tags.definition: In-app recording: cannot pause, auto-stops when backgrounded, fails to start.
positive_examples: 'cannot pause recording in app'
'recording auto-stops when backgrounded'

tags.definition: Importing external audio: format unsupported, quality degraded, fails, or size/length limit.
positive_examples: 'cannot import MP3; upload fails'
'format not supported on import'

tags.definition: App update fails, breaks/disconnects, removes a feature, or too slow (not firmware).
positive_examples: 'app update fails'
'update removed a feature'

tags.definition: No/poor folders, poor naming/dating, inadequate sorting, no bulk actions.
positive_examples: 'no folder system / poor sorting'
'no bulk actions on files'

tags.definition: Edits not saved, hard to correct, find&replace broken, cannot rename, low-confidence not flagged.
positive_examples: 'edits to transcript not saved'
'find & replace broken; cannot rename file'

tags.definition: No dark mode, weak notification controls, limited personalization, no battery level in app.
positive_examples: 'no dark mode'
'cannot see device battery in app'

tags.definition: Cannot turn off in-app ads / upgrade promotion pop-ups.
positive_examples: 'cannot turn off in-app ads/promotions'

tags.definition: No read-aloud/screen-reader; text size or contrast insufficient.
positive_examples: 'no screen-reader support'
'text size/contrast insufficient'

tags.definition: Desktop limited vs mobile, no Linux, virtual audio driver conflict, no screen-record or speaker-name capture.
positive_examples: 'desktop limited vs mobile / no Linux'
'cannot screen-record; audio driver conflict'

tags.definition: No dedicated iPad app, iPhone-mode poor scaling, landscape unsupported.
positive_examples: 'no iPad app; runs in iPhone mode'
'landscape unsupported'

tags.definition: No in-app feature introduction; profile setup friction at first launch.
positive_examples: 'no in-app feature introduction'
'profile setup friction at first launch'

tags.definition: New-account creation stage: whether a user can successfully register a new account and pass email / OTP verification. Covers ONLY failures creating an account from scratch — not login on an existing account.
positive_examples: 'The email verification code never arrives to my Apple relay alias'
'Codes I enter are rejected as incorrect'
'System treats my existing email as unregistered and forces new account creation'

mece_rules.reason: Reset / lost-credential is Recovery, not registration

negative_examples.example: 'Password reset verification codes are not received'

tags.definition: Authentication stage: for an existing account, failures between entering credentials and a successful login (credentials rejected, SSO failure, login flow error/stuck, account locked). Only 'why THIS login attempt failed'.
positive_examples: 'Wrong account or password, but the same credentials work on mobile'
'Google sign-in loop, cannot authenticate'
'Login page white-screens / crashes'
'Too many attempts, account locked'

mece_rules.reason: Wants to change/switch login method (is already in)
Session dropped after a successful login

negative_examples.example: 'Forgot the old password and the reset flow is broken'
'Cannot switch from Apple SSO to email login'

tags.definition: Recovery stage: the user has lost credentials or account-identity info (password reset, forgotten registration email/method, manual back-office recovery) and needs to regain access. It includes users who have simply lost their own credentials/identity.
positive_examples: 'Forgot which email I used and the reset link is invalid'
'Forgot password and the forgot-password flow errors out'
'Do not remember whether I signed up with Google or Apple'

mece_rules.reason: Asset is on a different/other account

negative_examples.example: 'Device is bound to my father's account'
'Want to transfer the account to a colleague'

tags.definition: Attribute-change stage: the user CAN access the account but wants to change the login method or account attributes (change login email, switch/add login method, region/country correction). User is 'in'; the ask is to 'change'.
positive_examples: 'Change primary login email to my work Outlook address'
'Switch from Apple SSO to email+password'
'Registered under wrong country via VPN, need region corrected'

mece_rules.reason: The login method itself fails (cannot get in)
Changing email to hand the account to another person

tags.definition: Session-maintenance stage: authentication succeeded, but keeping the session or reusing login state across surfaces (unexpected logout, Web/desktop login, third-party connector authorization) fails.
positive_examples: 'App logs me out every few days'
'Web says my email is not registered though the app works'
'Clicking Launch Plaud Desktop does nothing'
'MCP connector only offers Google/email, my Apple account cannot authorize'

negative_examples.example: 'After logout, Google SSO now fails with a loop'

tags.definition: Account termination/handover axis: deletion requests, post-deletion residual issues, and transfer of an account between people (offboarding, gifting, changing the responsible owner). Focus on the account entity's existence and change of owner.
positive_examples: 'Please delete my account and data'
'After deletion my device is still linked to the deleted account'
'Employee left, re-bind the company account to a new owner'

mece_rules.reason: User changes their OWN email, same person
Transfer subscription only -> Monetization > Plan Transfer

negative_examples.example: 'I want to change my own login email'
'Transfer only my subscription, not the account'

tags.definition: Security axis: the fact or fear of UNAUTHORIZED access to the account (suspected compromise, abnormal access). Here the worry is someone ELSE getting in.
positive_examples: 'I see abnormal login activity / my content changed'
'My Google account was hacked and now my PLAUD access is affected'

mece_rules.reason: Plain login failure, no compromise signs
2FA/security settings requests & data-storage concerns -> Security & Privacy

tags.definition: Catch-all for Account & Login; use when no other account and login tag applies.
